To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) modern CS observations can only be reconciled with a stiff EoS for nuclear matter, (ii) a stiff EoS can only be realized in a hybrid EoS, and (iii) a hybrid EoS with a 2SC quark matter core is compatible with modern CS observations

the quark matter EoS is consistent both with the maximum mass constraint and the large radii of the most compact stars and that a hybrid star with a quark matter core is consistent with the mass-radius relation of all known CS.

(i) modern CS observations are consistent with a deconfining phase transition at ∼0.55 fm−3, (ii) hybrid stars with a 2SC quark core can be consistent with modern CS constraints and (iii) hybrid stars with CFL cores cannot be consistent with modern compact star constraints.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues.
the question of how to reconcile the high CS masses with a first order phase transition to quark matter at low density.

the construction of an EoS that satisfies phenomenological input from CS observations, heavy-ion collisions, and nuclear matter calculations, which can serve as a starting point for further investigations of CS physics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
modern compact star observations do not provide any evidence that quark matter is present at high densities in the cores of compact stars.
the EoS is not known with sufficient precision to make a definite statement on the existence of quark matter in compact stars.
a hybrid EoS is required in order to describe the phenomenology of modern CS observations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quark matter phase in the present model is too stiff and the quark core too small to have any significant impact on neutron star properties.
a hybrid star equation of state with a quark core in the 2SC phase is favored by modern CS observations.
the quark matter EoS in the present hybrid EoS is not stiff enough to produce stable hybrid stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a quark matter EoS that accounts for vector interactions and diquark condensates in the presence of vector meson fields can be consistent with CS observations and heavy-ion collision data, while the corresponding nuclear matter phase is consistent with nuclear phenomenology and the DBHF approach.
the EoS for the nuclear phase has to be stiff in order to accommodate the high masses and radii of modern CS observations.
a hybrid EoS with a 2SC quark core is compatible with modern observations and that the 2SC phase transition can be driven by the vector meson coupling.
